checks_passed.what_was_verified: All three [IMAGE_EXTRACT] spans, at lines 74, 76 and 78, were checked against the rendered page image input/pages/p04.png. Formula (I) is drawn as the 2-benzoylcyclohexane-1,3-dione with a ring CH at C2; the SMILES CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)C2C(=O)CCCC2=O)c(Cl)c1COCC(F)(F)F encodes exactly that. Aryl substituent positions were read off the page and not inferred: benzoyl at C1, Cl at C2, CH2-O-CH2-CF3 at C3, SO2CH3 at C4, which is what the SMILES ring closure order c1(SO2Me) c c c(benzoyl) c(Cl) c1(CH2O) gives and what the printed name requires. (I') is drawn with OH on a ring carbon and the exocyclic C=O intact, matching C2=C(O)CCCC2=O with C(=O) outside the ring. (I'') is drawn with OH on the exocyclic carbon and both ring carbonyls intact, matching C(O)=C2C(=O)CCCC2=O. All three read C17H16ClF3O6S by hand count. No reaction scheme and no arrow appears anywhere in the document, so there is no above-arrow and below-arrow merge to check, and no background scheme was annotated as the invention's route. The three drawing-sheet sections correctly hold zero compounds: pages p02 and p03 carry only diffractograms, whose axis labels 2-Theta and Intensity (CPS) name no substance, and the figure-to-form mapping was correctly taken from [0068] to [0070] rather than from the sheets.

The parts-by-weight compositions of the ten formulation examples were summed against the page. I: 20+3+17+60=100. II: 5+95=100. III: 20+2+8+2+68=100. IV: 20+10+70=100. V: 10+17+2+1+7+63=100. No step in this patent states a product mass or a yield, so there is no yield closure to test and no step-to-step mass continuity: nothing in the document synthesises tembotrione.

Every one of the 305 distinct identifiers was traced to a printed line. Ninety-two identifiers are not printed verbatim in their cited lines; of those, eighty-two carry the printed string as an alias, and the remaining ten are the crystal-form records whose sections name the form only by a letter in a table column or in a combined phrase, which the notes state explicitly. No record is unanchored and no fabrication was found. In particular no condition, atmosphere or default was invented: the A1 schema carries no conditions field. No record carries a smiles, molecular_formula, molecular_weight, id, compound_uuid, enrichment or vector field; the field set is identical across all 497 records. Three SMILES strings do appear, in the aliases of the single formula-I record only, which A1 rule 4b requires and rule 4c satisfies by leaving no structure field, so this is not a forbidden structure assertion.

Of 501 provenance quotes, 500 are byte-present in the cited line span once the 'NNNN | ' prefix is stripped and the '    > EN: ' lines are excluded from the corpus. The prefix strip was performed first, so the check actually excludes the EN lines; without it the corpus would have contained every EN line and the check would have passed vacuously. The single failure is reported as a finding.

The dense lists were enumerated by hand off the page and diffed against the artifact. Colorants at line 600: all thirty distinct names are present, from Rhodamin B through Basic Red 108, including the four Pigment Blue 15:x shades and the four Pigment Red x:y shades; the source prints 'Basic Red 10' twice and the artifact correctly holds one record. Non-ionic surfactants at line 581: all twenty-eight enumerated members present, including the split of 'di- and tristyrylphenol alkoxylates' into two records and of the di- and tri-block copolymers into two. Protective colloids at line 583: all sixteen enumerated members present. Binders at line 602: all thirty-nine enumerated members present. Fillers at line 604 and plasticizers at line 606: all present. Solid carriers at lines 564 and 637: all twenty-four present, with 'calcium and magnesium sulfate' and 'wood and nutshell flour' correctly split into two records each with the printed phrase kept as an alias. Buffer acids at line 622: all nine present. Non-aqueous phase components at line 629 and water-miscible solvents at line 610: all present. Nonpolar antisolvents at line 214: all nine present. Where a class name has enumerated members under it, the artifact consistently emits the members and not the umbrella; that policy is applied uniformly across the formulation sections.

The source is an English-language US national-phase publication, so check 5 was run as a page-versus-record comparison. Every compound name in the artifact was compared against what the page prints. The artifact follows the page in every case where the page and the PDF text layer differ, and it says so: H2O rather than the text layer's HO in TABLE 2, 'acetone' rather than 'acetOne' in TABLE 5, 'B + C' rather than 'B - C' in TABLES 3 and 4, 'dimethyl sulfoxide' as two words. Naming conflicts inside the patent are recorded and not resolved: the 2,2-dimethylpropanol and tert. amyl alcohol gloss at lines 291 and 303 is kept unresolved with a note that the two are different C5H12O alcohols; the 'methyl ethyl ketone' and 'ethyl methyl ketone' word-order split is unified on the description form with the table form as an alias; the malformed claim 16 name 'trifluoroethoxymethyebenzoyl' is transcribed as printed with the defect noted; 'dioxan' is kept in the printed spelling rather than corrected to dioxane; 'terbuthylazin' is kept without the usual final e. No name was silently repaired.

The A1 CompoundRecord carries no precursor_step and no linkage_confirmed field, so check 6 has no target in this artifact. The nearest substitute was tested instead: for each of the eighteen records with role reactant, the section does state a transformation consuming that substance, and for each of the thirty-four with role product the section does state its formation. The three-form reactant and product assignments in the stability study at lines 523 to 531 are correct: form B is the consumed form, forms A and C are the produced forms, and the contradiction between a B-containing mixture going to A and pure B going to C is recorded rather than resolved.

All 497 records were checked field by field against the A1 closed lists. role: only product, reactant, reagent, solvent, catalyst, ligand, base, acid, oxidant, reductant, by_product, additive, drying_agent, other are allowed and only product, reactant, solvent, acid, additive and other occur. identifier_type: only iupac, trivial_name and other occur, all in the list. physical_form: only crystals and null occur, both allowed. analytics method: only xrd and dsc occur, both in the list. Every record carries exactly one compound_class tag and every value is in the thirteen-item list. Every tag is category:value with a lowercase snake_case ASCII value and no duplicates; there are no physical_form, color, role_seen or commercial tags. The only hazard tag is hazard:toxic on the two tetrachloromethane records, which the prompt mandates. No record has a case mismatch except the deliberate upper-case S in S-metolachlor, which the notes justify as a stereodescriptor.

All 497 records carry the identical twenty-three-key field set and nothing else: patent_id, identifier, identifier_type, aliases, resolved, unresolved_reference, section_label, section_type, is_section_product, commercially_available, role, quantity, ms_mz, nmr, melting_point, appearance, color, physical_form, analytics, purity_pct, purity_method, tags, notes. No id, compound_uuid, smiles or enrichment field is present. patent_id is US20100041557A1 on every record. Every section_label and section_type pair matches the A0 section map. No section file has a duplicate identifier, so the one-record-per-compound-per-section merge rule holds. Unset characterisation fields are null rather than empty objects. The five zero-length section files each ship a provenance entry with identifier null explaining that the section was read and names no compound, which is the right way to distinguish a read-and-empty section from a missing one. A1 has no validation_flag field, so the internal inconsistencies the artifact found are carried in notes, which is the only place available.
